request: не слишком гладко можно чтобы ланшафт был не такой сложный и в пиксельном стиле
scope: Preview-only simplification/redraw of two previous scenes. No runtime integration.
prompts:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: corrected pixel-art tactical scene preview, one image, same 1448x1086 framing as input.
Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, the prior scene concept. User feedback: the landscape is much too smooth, too elaborate, and needs simple PIXEL ART. Redraw the BATTLEFIELD TERRAIN and environmental effects in deliberately simple crisp pixel art while preserving the established restrained palette. This must be a very obvious change in terrain rendering and detail density, not a tiny filter.
TOP PRIORITY: hand-authored connected pixel clusters. Ground tiles should feel drawn at about 48x36 logical pixels per top diamond, then nearest-neighbor enlarged ~2x. Clearly visible consistent 2-3 screen pixel square steps at edges and highlights. ONLY 2-3 flat shades per material. Large calm color regions. Short hard-edged pixel staircases. No subpixel softening, no antialiasing on terrain, no smooth gradients, no blurry texture, no photographic water, no realistic materials, no tiny noise or dithering, no rounded vector-art sheen, no bevel highlights on every tile.
A single broad surface per gameplay cell: do not subdivide stone tiles into lots of tiny bricks. Use fine restrained grid boundaries, no thick dark outline on every floor tile. Ground is mostly quiet; almost all decorative speckles, cracks, stones, grass tufts and reeds must disappear. Keep very few simple coherent pixel grass clumps.
Land tops: #64785A shade, #7D9270 base, #98A286 small light patches. Earth: #685844 shade, #92775B sides, #978971 mid, #A6967B dry patches. Stone: #5D7078 shade, #9DADB0 light, neutral grey-blue intermediate flat plane. Two broad flat bands on exposed brown sides; NO strata striping or repeated microtexture.
Water: #3E6570 shade, #527F87 body, #86AAA8 a handful of short angular pixel reflection marks over the entire water body. Mostly completely flat dark blue-teal surface. No thin curvy ripple web, foam, caustics, gradients, shiny flowing waterfall, or transparent realistic depth.
Acid: #7DAC73 base, #ADD6AA light with a small #BDCF86 yellow-green accent, flat opaque angular puddle silhouette, 2 small stepped pixel bubbles only. Easily separated from darker bluish water and muted grass.
Fire: #B9604E dark, #D58E4F orange, #ECC577 center, three or four chunky stepped flame shapes, no smooth teardrop curves or bloom.
Deep contours #202C31. Keep #293C48 dark background, #314754 UI, #E7E6D6/#B2C0C3 text, #D3AD6A active action, #84B6A6 selection, #8E7FA4/#C3B9D2 violet rune.
LOCK: same scene identity, steep 4:3 top diamond projection (not shallow 2:1), broad battlefield position/scale, warm brown soil sides, six existing character identities, their poses, scale and positions, their visible feet/contact shadows and health/resource bars. Keep HUD, all words/buttons, fonts and surrounding background unchanged as closely as possible. Do NOT simply pixelate the entire screenshot: fonts/UI remain smooth original UI, characters remain unchanged, the TERRAIN must be freshly simplified and drawn in pixel clusters. No title, labels, swatch grid, or side-by-side comparison. This remains preview-only, not implemented game content.
SCENE-SPECIFIC: simplify the grassland ford. Keep one narrow blue-teal river separating two open grassy banks in roughly the current position, simplify banks to a few long rectilinear grid-aligned steps, without tiny jutting peninsula shapes. Keep the same simple bridge crossing, rendered as three broad flat wooden planks with 2-3 straight seams total, no fine grain. Keep one low raised grass block in the back, remove the extra raised block. Remove every shore boulder and nearly all reeds, retain at most TWO tiny square-cluster grass tufts near the bank. Most tiles have just one quiet grass fill; a few have ONE large sparse earth patch, not mottled repeated texture. Keep the one acid puddle, one fire, one spike trap and one squat obstacle at approximately their current positions. Trap is a simple flat plate with 4 chunky pixel spikes; obstacle is a plain cube with a couple of large metal planes, no ornate lid or rivet pattern. No waterfall off the front edge, just a dark flat water end face. Open, simple, sparse, unmistakably pixel art.
